results.problem: Among Jakks Pacific, Hasbro, Mattel, and Funko which company had the highest debt-to-capital ratio for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023? Use the SEC website and filings.
results.answer_text:
Using the standard formula:

\[
\text{Debt-to-capital ratio}=\frac{\text{total debt}}{\text{total debt}+\text{stockholders' equity}}
\]

and the amounts reported in SEC filings for December 31, 2023:

| Company | Total debt | Stockholders’ equity | Debt-to-capital |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| JAKKS Pacific | Essentially no interest-bearing debt | $190.1M | ~0% |
| Hasbro | $3,465.8M carrying amount | $1,087.0M | **76.1%** |
| Mattel | $2,330.0M | $2,149.2M | 52.0% |
| Funko | $273.6M | $238.0M | 53.5% |

Notes:

- Hasbro debt is the balance-sheet carrying amount: $500.0M current debt plus $2,965.8M long-term debt. Its filing also reports $3,484.9M in principal debt; using that amount would produce a similar ratio of 76.2%.
- Funko debt includes its $120.5M line of credit, $22.1M current long-term debt, and $131.0M noncurrent long-term debt.
- SEC sources: [Hasbro 2023 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/46080/000004608024000034/has-20231231.htm), [Mattel 2023 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63276/000162828024011371/mat-20231231.htm), [Funko 2023 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1704711/000170471124000013/fnko-20231231.htm), and [JAKKS SEC filing containing the audited 2023 comparative balance sheet](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1009829/000118518525000170/jakk10k123124.htm).

**Final answer: Hasbro had the highest debt-to-capital ratio, at approximately 76.1%.**
